title: Understanding MSE Components
text: The Mean Squared Error (MSE) is composed of three parts: the squared bias, the variance, and the irreducible error. Each of these components contributes to the overall error in different ways.

title: Analyzing the Graph
text: Look at how the squared bias and variance change with model complexity. Notice that as model complexity increases, the squared bias decreases while the variance increases.

title: Irreducible Error
text: The irreducible error is constant and does not change with model complexity. It represents the noise inherent in the data that cannot be reduced by any model.

hintAnswer: The MSE is the sum of the squared model bias, the model variance and the irreducible error; it is approximately U shaped and its minimum occurs at the minimum of that curve.
title: Identifying the MSE Minimum
text: Where does the MSE reach its minimum on the graph? Consider the point where the sum of squared bias, variance, and irreducible error is lowest.
choices: The MSE is the sum of the squared model bias and the model variance only; its minimum occurs at the smallest model complexity.
The MSE is the sum of the squared model bias, the model variance and the irreducible error; it is approximately U shaped and its minimum occurs at the minimum of that curve.
The MSE is the difference between the model variance and the squared model bias; its minimum occurs where those two curves cross.
The MSE equals the irreducible error alone; it is a horizontal line and has no single minimum.
The MSE is the sum of the squared model bias, the model variance and the irreducible error; its minimum occurs at the largest model complexity.
